chapters.title: Everything Gets to You
chapters.tease: It isn't that you're fragile. It's that everything now has a way in.

chapters.title: The Tuesday That Ate the Week
chapters.tease: A comment lasts seconds. The replays can take your whole week, unless you close the file.

chapters.title: Your Mind Is a Group Chat
chapters.tease: Your thoughts are messages, not orders. You can read them without replying to all of them.

chapters.title: The Overthinking Tax
chapters.tease: Every problem has a price. Overthinking adds a tax on top, and it's usually the bigger bill.

chapters.title: Why Willpower Keeps Losing
chapters.tease: Your resolve is tested when you're tired, in a room set up for the opposite. Change the room.

chapters.title: The Phone Is Not Neutral
chapters.tease: Your phone was set up by people who want your attention. Set it up again for you.

chapters.title: Other People's Weather
chapters.tease: Most moods in the room aren't about you. Carry an umbrella; don't take the rain personally.

chapters.title: The Myth of the Clear Head
chapters.tease: Clarity rarely comes first. It usually turns up after the first small step.

chapters.title: Two Words on a Sticky Note
chapters.tease: The phrase was born on a night shift in Leeds. It's been stuck to a locker door ever since.

chapters.title: How to Read This Book
chapters.tease: Read it in order once, then dip in when something gets to you. Always do the box.

chapters.title: Noted: The First Word
chapters.tease: One word that ends the argument with what has already happened.

chapters.title: Name It to Shrink It
chapters.tease: A worry with a name and an edge is smaller than a worry with neither.

chapters.title: Don't Argue With the Weather
chapters.tease: Stop spending effort on the one thing effort can't touch.

chapters.title: The Receipt, Not the Essay
chapters.tease: Record what happened in four lines, then put it in the drawer.

chapters.title: Feelings Are Messengers, Not Managers
chapters.tease: Read the news a feeling brings. Don't let it make the decisions.

chapters.title: The Three-Second Pause
chapters.tease: Three seconds between the trigger and your reply turns a reflex into a choice.

chapters.title: Noted Is Not Agreed
chapters.tease: You can record a comment without voting for it.

chapters.title: Write It Down, Close the Loop
chapters.tease: Give every circling thought a line on paper, a next action and a day.

chapters.title: The Body Notices First
chapters.tease: Your body raises the alarm before your thoughts do, so look there first.

chapters.title: When Noted Isn't Enough
chapters.tease: Noted is first aid. Some things need more, and asking is the method at full strength.

chapters.title: Next: The Second Word
chapters.tease: Noted gets you out of the argument. Next gets you back into the room.

chapters.title: The Smallest Next Step
chapters.tease: Most procrastination is a sizing error. Shrink the step until your foot fits the stair.

chapters.title: Two Minutes, Then Decide
chapters.tease: Give the task two honest minutes, then choose: finish it, book it or hand it on.

chapters.title: Motion Before Motivation
chapters.tease: Motivation is a late guest. Start the motion and it usually turns up.

chapters.title: If This, Then Next
chapters.tease: Decide your next on a calm afternoon, so your tired self only has to recognise the cue.

chapters.title: The Next Step Is Usually Boring
chapters.tease: The step that excites you is often standing in front of the one that would help.

chapters.title: Next, Not Everything
chapters.tease: Your list is a car park. Everything is parked; only one thing is being driven.

chapters.title: Finish Lines Are Made of Nexts
chapters.tease: Stop measuring the distance left. Start counting the steps you have taken.

chapters.title: When You Don't Know What's Next
chapters.tease: 'I don't know what's next' usually means something specific is missing. Find it.

chapters.title: The Noted–Next Loop
chapters.tease: Six states, one breath: the whole method as a small machine you can carry anywhere.

chapters.title: The Three Rooms
chapters.tease: Every problem lives in one of three rooms. Next only ever happens in yours.

chapters.title: Room One: Yours
chapters.tease: Your room holds four things. That sounds small until you see what they can move.

chapters.title: Room Two: Theirs
chapters.tease: Love doesn't give you a key to someone else's room. It does give you plenty to do in yours.

chapters.title: Room Three: Weather
chapters.tease: You can't argue with weather. You can read the forecast, find a coat and get on with your day.

chapters.title: The Doorway Question
chapters.tease: One breath at the threshold: is this mine, theirs, or nobody's?

chapters.title: Worry Is Rent on the Wrong Room
chapters.tease: Worry feels like work. Mostly it's rent paid on a room you can't live in.

chapters.title: The Influence Corridor
chapters.tease: Ask, offer, persuade. Then do the hardest part: leave the corridor.

chapters.title: Moving Out of Their Room
chapters.tease: You can love someone without lodging in their opinion of you.

chapters.title: The Weather Report
chapters.tease: Give your own weather report each morning. Then stop checking the sky.

chapters.title: Living in Your Own Room
chapters.tease: Visit the other rooms as often as you like. Live in yours.

chapters.title: Their Opinion Is Their Furniture
chapters.tease: Other people's opinions live in their room. You can visit without carrying the sofa home.

chapters.title: The Group Chat You Didn't Join
chapters.tease: Being mentioned in a room you never entered is not a summons to enter it.

chapters.title: Noted, Not Absorbed
chapters.tease: You can see someone's storm clearly without letting it rain inside you.

chapters.title: The Conversation Under the Conversation
chapters.tease: Most rows have two layers. Answer the words, and listen for the weight under them.

chapters.title: Ask, Don't Assume
chapters.tease: A question costs a few seconds. An assumption can cost you the whole day.

chapters.title: Boundaries Are Doors, Not Walls
chapters.tease: A wall says go away. A door says here's how to reach me.

chapters.title: The Courage to Be Mildly Unpopular
chapters.tease: Being liked by everyone is a full-time job with no salary. Mild unpopularity is cheaper.

chapters.title: Families Have Long Memories
chapters.tease: Families keep an old photograph of you. You don't have to stand in front of it.

chapters.title: Apologise Once, Properly
chapters.tease: One proper apology is a gift. Twelve nervous ones are a burden.

chapters.title: The Generous Reading
chapters.tease: When you don't know why someone did it, choose the kindest plausible reason first.

chapters.title: You Fall to Your Settings
chapters.tease: The person who makes the plan is not the person who keeps it. Settings decide.

chapters.title: Design the Room, Not the Resolve
chapters.tease: Every room gives advice. Change the advice instead of arguing with it nightly.

chapters.title: The Friction Dial
chapters.tease: Add steps to what you want less of. Remove steps from what you want more of.

chapters.title: The First Ten Minutes
chapters.tease: The first ten minutes set the direction the rest of the hour leans in.

chapters.title: You Become What You Repeat
chapters.tease: Identity isn't where habits start. It's what they leave behind.

chapters.title: Anchor It to Something Solid
chapters.tease: 'When I have a minute' is a hope. Tie new habits to moments that already happen.

chapters.title: Give the Phone a New Address
chapters.tease: Your keys have a hook. Give the phone a home too, then visit it.

chapters.title: The Rule of the Second Day
chapters.tease: One missed day is weather. The day after decides what becomes your setting.

chapters.title: Shrink It Until It's Silly
chapters.tease: If a task won't start, it's too big. Shrink it until starting makes you laugh.

chapters.title: Defaults for Bad Days
chapters.tease: Bad days switch off the planner in you. Write the plan on a good day.

chapters.title: Calm Is Partly Plumbing
chapters.tease: Before you diagnose your life, check the pipes: sleep, food, water, light and movement.

chapters.title: Sleep Is the Overnight Edit
chapters.tease: Night thoughts are drafts, not verdicts. Write one line, then let sleep do the editing.

chapters.title: Morning Light, Outside
chapters.tease: Let the day arrive before the feed does: daylight first, phone second.

chapters.title: The Long Exhale
chapters.tease: You can't order yourself to calm down, but you can breathe out slowly and let the body take the hint.

chapters.title: Walk It Off, Literally
chapters.tease: A thought you keep rereading wants movement, not another read. Walk the loop, bring back one Next.

chapters.title: Caffeine Has Opinions
chapters.tease: A racing heart after the fourth coffee is chemistry before it is a message about your life.

chapters.title: Hunger in Disguise
chapters.tease: Sudden fury at six o'clock is often hunger wearing a costume. Ask when you last ate.

chapters.title: Rhythm Beats Intensity
chapters.tease: A programme you can only keep on your best week isn't a programme. It's an event.

chapters.title: Rest Before You Break
chapters.tease: Your earliest signs of strain are quiet. Rest at amber, while it's still cheap.

chapters.title: A Protocol, Not a Personality
chapters.tease: A lot of what you call your personality is really your protocol. Write the list on a good day.

chapters.title: The Inbox Is Not Your Boss
chapters.tease: An email is a request, not an order. Read your inbox like post, not like a summons.

chapters.title: Fewer Things, Finished
chapters.tease: Busy is not the same as done. Close three things before you open a fourth.

chapters.title: The Slow Yes, the Quick No
chapters.tease: Swap the speeds: make your yes slow and your no quick, and stop writing cheques you haven't checked.

chapters.title: Meetings Are Weather Too
chapters.tease: You can't control the meeting. You can control what you carry out of it.

chapters.title: Feedback: Noted, Then Next
chapters.tease: Criticism arrives as a sting before it arrives as sense. Write the receipt, sort the pile, change one thing.

chapters.title: Deep Hours
chapters.tease: You don't lack time for the work that matters. You lack unbroken time. Book it, and guard it.

chapters.title: The Comparison Feed
chapters.tease: The feed shows you their shop window. You live in your own stockroom. That's not a fair contest.

chapters.title: When the Machines Arrive at Work
chapters.tease: The agents can draft the reply. Only you can decide what you mean. Keep the judgement in Room One.

chapters.title: Ambition Without Anxiety
chapters.tease: Aim at the summit, but judge your week by the steps. That's ambition without the 2 a.m. hum.

chapters.title: Clocking Off Is a Skill
chapters.tease: Work ends when your mind believes it's parked somewhere safe, not when you leave the building.

chapters.title: Bad News Arrives Uninvited
chapters.tease: In the first hour after bad news you get three jobs, and deciding your whole future isn't one of them.

chapters.title: Money Worry at 3 a.m.
chapters.tease: Money worry feels like planning at 3 a.m. It isn't. Give it a pad, a daylight hour and, if needed, an adviser.

chapters.title: Failing in Public
chapters.tease: A public failure is a pile of comments, not a verdict. Sort the pile and some of it turns out to be free.

chapters.title: Grief Doesn't Take Notes
chapters.tease: Grief won't follow a method. Noted gives it permission; Next stays body-sized and kind.

chapters.title: Illness and the Long Wait
chapters.tease: In a long medical wait the answer isn't in your room yet, but the days still are.

chapters.title: When Someone Leaves
chapters.tease: Their leaving is their decision. Rebuilding the shape of your week is yours.

chapters.title: The Setback Ledger
chapters.tease: Memory keeps the sting and loses the ending. A ledger keeps both.

chapters.title: Panic Has a Shape
chapters.tease: Panic feels endless. It has a shape: it rises, peaks and falls. Name the shape and ride it.

chapters.title: Asking for Help Is a Next
chapters.tease: Asking for help isn't the white flag after the method fails. It is the method.

chapters.title: The Day After the Worst Day
chapters.tease: The day after the worst day isn't for verdicts. It's for water, daylight and one small thing at a time.

chapters.title: Unbothered Is Not Uncaring
chapters.tease: Calm isn't caring less. It's caring with your hands instead of your stomach.

chapters.title: Meaning Lives in the Next
chapters.tease: You don't find meaning by hunting for it. You build it one chosen step at a time.

chapters.title: The Life-Sized Life
chapters.tease: The feed gives you a planet-sized life and ant-sized hands. Choose a life the size you can tend.

chapters.title: Enough
chapters.tease: If you don't draw your own finish line, someone selling something will draw it for you.

chapters.title: Small Joys on Purpose
chapters.tease: Joy rarely kicks the door down. Book it in, and learn to notice when it knocks.

chapters.title: Teach It to Someone
chapters.tease: Explain it once to someone who needs it, and you'll understand it twice.

chapters.title: The Long Game of Small Days
chapters.tease: You won't see yourself change. One day you'll notice that you have.

chapters.title: Who You Are When Nothing Happens
chapters.tease: Most of us are well rehearsed for trouble. Fewer of us know what to do with a quiet afternoon.

chapters.title: Find Your Own Two Words
chapters.tease: These two words were borrowed. The best ones you'll ever use will be your own.

chapters.title: Noted. Next.
chapters.tease: Things will keep getting to you. Two words decide what happens after that.
